place_text: House Oversight Committee hearing, Washington, D.C.

as_told.title: Elizondo declines to confirm Immaculate Constellation at congressional hearing

tellings.page: Questioning by Ms. Mace, second round
tellings.quote: Ma'am, I would not be authorized to confirm nor deny the existence of any ongoing or past program, especially as it relates to a special access program, either by name or trigraph.

plain: At a House Oversight Committee hearing on 13 November 2024, Representative Nancy Mace asked Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official known for speaking publicly about AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, whether he had been given access to an alleged secret program called Immaculate Constellation. The hearing record has him answer: "I would not be authorized to confirm nor deny the existence of any ongoing or past program, especially as it relates to a special access program, either by name or trigraph". A special access program is a tightly restricted classified program, and a trigraph is a three-letter code name. Michels calls this "a very interesting answer", and a later episode replays Elizondo's words, since they could hint that he knew of it. The program is named in an anonymous report that the journalist Michael Shellenberger gave to Congress and Mace entered into the hearing record. The report calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report. A former Defense Department official named Matthew Brown later said he wrote it, and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of such a program. The report ties Elizondo to AATIP, saying the program was set up "following the public disclosure of the AATIP/AAWSAP programs by Luis Elizondo in 2017", but it does not take up whether he himself was ever read into the program.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report names Luis Elizondo twice: the program was "established following the public disclosure of the AATIP/AAWSAP programs by Luis Elizondo in 2017", and internal records "confirm the claims of Mr. Lue Elizondo regarding AATIP/AAWSAP's mission, activities, and findings". Both tie him to AATIP; whether he was read into Immaculate Constellation itself is the question Rep. Nancy Mace put to him at the hearing, and the report does not take it up.
